thin-provision.name: Thin provisioning
thin-provision.title: Thin provisioning recommendation
thin-provision.description: Workload Factory recommends configuring thin provisioning for FSx for ONTAP volumes hosting Oracle databases. This approach optimizes storage efficiency and cost-effectiveness by allowing more logical data to be stored than physically available.

autosize.name: Autosize
autosize.title: Autosize recommendation
autosize.description: Workload Factory recommends enabling volume autogrow for FSx for ONTAP volumes for Oracle databases. This configuration enhances flexibility, availability, and scalability for Oracle databases by allowing volumes to grow dynamically to accommodate unexpected data growth, preventing space shortages and avoiding downtime if a volume runs out of space. Volume autogrow is essential when using thin provisioning.

autosize-mode.name: Autosize mode
autosize-mode.title: Autosize mode recommendation
autosize-mode.description: Workload Factory recommends enabling volume autogrow for FSx for ONTAP volumes for Oracle databases. This configuration enhances flexibility and availability by allowing volumes to grow dynamically to accommodate unexpected data growth. This prevents space shortages and helps avoid downtime if a volume runs out of space, ensuring seamless scalability for Oracle databases. Volume autogrow is essential when using thin provisioning.

snapshot-policy.name: Snapshot policy
snapshot-policy.title: Snapshot policy recommendation
snapshot-policy.description: Workload Factory recommends disabling snapshots for FSx for ONTAP volumes for Oracle databases to save space and lower costs. Oracle snapshots should be managed externally via tools like SnapCenter, which creates application-consistent snapshots, preventing corruption during restoration.

snapshot-copy-reserve.name: Snapshot copy reserve
snapshot-copy-reserve.title: Snapshot copy reserve recommendation
snapshot-copy-reserve.description: Workload Factory recommends that capacity isn't reserved for snapshots on FSx for ONTAP volumes used by databases, making the entire volume capacity available for active data and any snapshots that are created.

snapshot-autodelete.name: Snapshot autodelete
snapshot-autodelete.title: Snapshot autodelete recommendation
snapshot-autodelete.description: Workload Factory recommends configuring the snapshot autodelete feature in FSx for ONTAP for Oracle databases to delete older snapshots first. This feature is designed to automatically manage snapshot storage by deleting the oldest snapshots when a volume approaches its capacity limit. This configuration helps in thin-provisioned environments, where more logical storage is allocated than physically available.

space-mgmt-try-first.name: Space management try first
space-mgmt-try-first.title: Space management try first recommendation
space-mgmt-try-first.description: Workload Factory recommends configuring space management to prioritize volume expansion over snapshot deletion for thin-provisioned FSx for ONTAP volumes with volume autogrow enabled.

nfs-rootonly.name: NFS rootonly
nfs-rootonly.title: NFS rootonly recommendation
nfs-rootonly.description: Workload Factory recommends disabling the nfs-rootonly parameter for dNFS. ONTAP's nfs-rootonly setting restricts NFS connections to privileged ports (<1024). Since dNFS processes in NFSv4+ do not run as root and use higher ports, disabling this parameter allows necessary connections.

export-policy.name: Export policy
export-policy.title: Export policy recommendation
export-policy.description: Workload Factory recommends ensuring that If Oracle binaries are located on an NFS share, the export policy includes superuser and setuid permissions.Superuser (root) access allows NFS clients to map as root, needed for binary execution.

os-type.name: LUN OS type
os-type.title: LUN OS type recommendation
os-type.description: Workload Factory recommends ensuring that the ONTAP LUN operating system (OS) type value matches the operating system partionioning scheme to achieve I/O alignment. Incorrect configuration might reduce performance.

block-device-space-management.name: Block device space management
block-device-space-management.title: Block device space management recommendation
block-device-space-management.description:
Workload Factory recommends configuring block device space settings for LUNs used by Oracle instances to prevent write failures and improve space efficiency on FSx for ONTAP. This configuration applies the recommended combination of settings for thin‑provisioned volumes:
 Space reservation: enabled — reserves enough space in the volume so writes to the LUN don’t fail. 
 Space allocation: enabled — allows FSx for ONTAP to notify the EC2 host when a volume is full and supports automatic space reclamation when the database deletes data. 
 Fractional reserve: disabled — avoids unnecessary overwrite reservation, optimizing space utilization and cost effectiveness for thin provisioning.Together, these settings help ensure predictable database behavior while minimizing wasted capacity.

multipath-io.name: Multipath I/O
multipath-io.title: Multipath I/O recommendation
multipath-io.description: Workload Factory recommends enabling Multipath I/O (MPIO) on database hosts that connect to ISCSI LUNs for Oracle databases. This host-level configuration enhances storage reliability and performance by providing redundant data paths between the server and storage. With multipath enabled, the system can automatically reroute I/O operations in the event of a path failure, minimizing downtime and ensuring consistent access to critical data.

host-utilities.name: Host utilities
host-utilities.title: Host utilities recommendation
host-utilities.description: Workload Factory recommends installing host utilities for Oracle databases. This host-level configuration enhances storage reliability and performance by providing redundant data paths between the server and storage. With multipath enabled, the system can automatically reroute I/O operations in the event of a path failure, minimizing downtime and ensuring consistent access to critical data.

selinux.name: SELinux
selinux.title: SELinux recommendation
selinux.description: Workload Factory recommends disabling SELinux on Oracle database hosts by setting SELINUX=disabled in the system configuration. Disabling SELinux can help avoid compatibility issues and administrative overhead associated with managing SELinux policies for Oracle workloads. After this change, SELinux will no longer enforce access controls, so ensure that your environment is otherwise secured.

iscsi-replacement-timeout.name: iSCSI replacement timeout
iscsi-replacement-timeout.title: iSCSI replacement timeout recommendation
iscsi-replacement-timeout.description: Workload Factory recommends setting the iSCSI replacement timeout to 5 seconds on Oracle database hosts. This setting helps ensure that iSCSI connections are properly managed and can recover quickly from interruptions, minimizing potential downtime for database workloads.

swap-space.name: Swap space
swap-space.title: Swap space sizing recommendation
swap-space.description: Proper swap sizing ensures that the system can handle memory pressure gracefully, avoiding potential performance degradation or system crashes.
swap-space.valuesHeading: Swap space should be sized relatively to RAM:
values: Between 1 GB and 2 GB: 1.5 times the size of the RAM
Between 2 GB and 16 GB: Equal to the size of the RAM

file-system-headroom.name: File system headroom
file-system-headroom.title: File system headroom sizing recommendation
file-system-headroom.description: To optimize storage performance, provision file system capacity as 1.2 times of total size of provisioned volume.
file-system-headroom.valuesHeading: File system headroom percentages are as follows:

transparent-hugepages.name: Transparent HugePages
transparent-hugepages.title: Transparent HugePages recommendation
transparent-hugepages.description: Workload Factory recommends disabling Transparent HugePages (THP) on database hosts running Oracle databases. Disabling THP is an Oracle best practice to prevent potential performance issues and ensure optimal database stability.

tcp-advanced-options.name: TCP advanced options
tcp-advanced-options.title: TCP advanced options recommendation
tcp-advanced-options.description: Workload Factory recommends enabling TCP timestamps, SACK, and window scaling for best network performance and reliability.

filesystems-io-options.name: Filesystems I/O options
filesystems-io-options.title: Filesystems I/O options recommendation
filesystems-io-options.description: Workload Factory recommends setting filesystemio_options = setall for optimal I/O performance. Adjust SGA size if needed when moving away from buffered I/O.

multiblock-readcount.name: Multiblock read count
multiblock-readcount.title: Multiblock read count recommendation
multiblock-readcount.description: Workload Factory recommends removing db_file_multiblock_read_count from init.ora to prevent performance issues and allow Oracle to manage this setting automatically.

host_os_patch.name: Host OS patch
host_os_patch.title: Host OS patch recommendation
host_os_patch.description: Critical security patches are missing. We recommend applying the latest patches to ensure your Oracle database infrastructure is secure and up-to-date.

crr.name: Cross-region replication
crr.title: Cross-region replication recommendation
crr.description: Workload Factory recommends enabling Cross-Region Replication (CRR) for your FSx for ONTAP filesystems serving Oracle. CRR ensures that your data is replicated to another AWS region, providing enhanced data durability and availability. It is recommended to configure CRR for disaster recovery and compliance requirements. Replicating redo logs (when applicable) can also assist with recovery to a specific point in time.

clone-management.name: Clone management
clone-management.title: Clone management recommendation
clone-management.description: Old clones can incur significant costs. Consider deleting these clones to optimize your storage expenses.

snapcenter-snapshot.name: SnapCenter snapshot
snapcenter-snapshot.title: SnapCenter snapshot recommendation
snapcenter-snapshot.description: Application-consistent snapshots with NetApp SnapCenter enable you to capture precise, reliable point-in-time images of your data volumes, ensuring that your applications remain fully operational and data integrity is maintained. Use SnapCenter to streamline backup processes and facilitate rapid, accurate restores—minimizing downtime and safeguarding your business-critical workloads.

aws-backup.name: AWS Backup
aws-backup.title: AWS Backup recommendation
aws-backup.description: Backup Configuration recommendation: Enable FSx Backup or AWS Backup for Oracle volumes to support data retention and compliance. Avoid redundant backups to optimize costs.

oracle-security-patch.name: Oracle security patch
oracle-security-patch.title: Oracle security patch recommendation
oracle-security-patch.description: Oracle Critical Patch Updates (CPUs) include security fixes for supported self-managed Oracle databases. Installing the latest patch helps protect your database from vulnerabilities and improves system reliability.

storage-efficiencies.name: Storage Efficiencies
storage-efficiencies.title: Storage efficiencies recommendation
storage-efficiencies.description: Workload Factory recommends implementing storage efficiencies—compression, compaction, and deduplication—in NetApp ONTAP for Oracle database environments to significantly reduce storage footprint, lower costs, and optimize resource utilization while maintaining performance. Tailored settings for each volume type ensure alignment with Oracle’s I/O patterns: Data and archive Volumes benefit from inline adaptive compression (8KB), compaction and deduplication while Redo Log Volumes prioritize performance with minimal savings from these features.

tiering-tco-optimization.name: Tiering / TCO optimization
tiering-tco-optimization.title: Tiering / TCO optimization recommendation
tiering-tco-optimization.description: Workload Factory recommends enabling tiering for some Oracle database volumes on Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP where appropriate, to move cold data to lower-cost capacity storage and reduce overall storage costs, while keeping active database data on high-performance SSDs to preserve critical performance. Recommended policies are based on the data type in each volume, with tiering disabled (none) for data files and redo logs, and auto for archive logs. For archive/FRA volumes, it is also recommended to set an appropriate cooling period before data is tiered—typically 2 days for compressed backups and 14 days for uncompressed backups—to balance cost efficiency and performance.
